sources.title: Web Cryptography API — ECDSA operations
sections: 23.7 Sign / Verify / Generate Key / Export Key
normalizedFindings: P-256 key generation supports sign and verify usages. Signing uses the private key and selected digest; verification uses the public key and returns a boolean.
Generated public keys are extractable; the private key inherits the extractable argument. SPKI export encodes the public key and algorithm parameters.
sources.retrieval: Opened and inspected through web tool; cached normalized findings, not the full document.

sources.title: SubtleCrypto.generateKey
normalizedFindings: For asymmetric generation, extractable controls private-key export; public keys remain extractable. Requires a supporting secure context.
sources.retrieval: Opened and inspected through web tool; normalized relevant API documentation.

sources.title: SubtleCrypto.sign — ECDSA
normalizedFindings: ECDSA signs with a private key; the hash is supplied to sign(). The result is a signature buffer, not encrypted plaintext.
Web Crypto ECDSA signatures concatenate fixed-width r and s values; this differs from ASN.1 DER signatures.
sources.retrieval: Opened and inspected through web tool; normalized relevant API documentation.

sources.title: SubtleCrypto.verify
normalizedFindings: Verification consumes the key, algorithm, signature and original data, returning true or false. A supplied name is not an input authenticated by this API.
sources.retrieval: Opened and inspected through web tool; normalized relevant API documentation. Named-identity limit is an inference from inputs plus unbound generated keys.

sources.title: SubtleCrypto.exportKey
normalizedFindings: The spki format exports SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes. A public-key fingerprint can hash these exact bytes rather than PEM or base64 display text.
sources.retrieval: Opened and inspected through web tool; fingerprint convention is this lab design, not a separate API guarantee.

sources.title: SubtleCrypto.digest
sections: Converting a digest to a hex string
normalizedFindings: SHA-256 digests an input buffer to 256 bits. Hex is a display encoding of the digest. Hashing SPKI identifies that public-key encoding; hashing text identifies message bytes.
sources.retrieval: Opened and inspected through web tool; normalized relevant API documentation.

sources.title: Web Cryptography Level 2 — Security considerations for authors
sources.version: First Public Working Draft, 22 April 2025; not a Recommendation
normalizedFindings: Non-extractability does not promise hardware isolation, protected storage, or zeroization after references are dropped. Hostile scripts may still misuse accessible keys.
Keys are not automatically persisted by application code; lifecycle and storage promises require implementation review.
sources.retrieval: Inspected the redirected current W3C publication carrying this dated draft; draft status retained.

contract.messageEncoding: UTF-8 via TextEncoder; sign and verify the exact bytes without trimming or silent normalization.
contract.fingerprint: SHA-256 of the exact SPKI bytes; display the full 32-byte digest as hex, or explicitly mark a shortened preview.
contract.expectedSignatureFormat: P-256 Web Crypto result: 64-byte raw r || s (P1363), not DER.

claims.copy: A valid signature matches these exact message bytes and this public key.
The message stays readable. Signing does not encrypt it.
claims.basis: Signature output is separate from input message; no encryption operation is used.

claims.copy: This generated key is not linked to a verified person or account.
claims.basis: Application-design inference: this lab generates an unbound key pair; verification alone supplies no trusted identity binding.

claims.copy: The private key is non-extractable through the Web Crypto export API.
claims.basis: API restriction only; do not claim hardware security, impossible theft or guaranteed memory erasure.
Explicit lab encoding convention; not a certificate, biometric fingerprint or proof of a person.

suggestedCopy.heading: Sign a message. Change one character. Verify again.
suggestedCopy.description: Generate a browser signing key, create a signature, then test whether an edited message still matches.
suggestedCopy.valid: Signature valid for this message and public key.
suggestedCopy.invalid: Signature does not match this message and public key.
suggestedCopy.limits: This demonstration checks a message against a public key. It does not encrypt the message or verify a named person.

implementationDependentClaimsToVerify: No network requests from the proof operation.
No localStorage, IndexedDB or other application persistence of messages/keys.
Key references are dropped on reset/unmount; do not claim secure erasure.
Signing occurs only after an explicit visitor action.
Capability and operation failures show a truthful unsupported/error state.
Signing/loading results are discarded if the visitor edits or resets before completion.
suggestedChecks: Changed message, changed signature and wrong public key verify false.
Private-key export rejects; public SPKI export and fingerprint succeed.
A new key changes the fingerprint.
Unicode input is signed and checked as the same UTF-8 bytes.
Never treat a timestamp or unbound fingerprint as trusted identity, freshness or a certificate.
